question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[{e}^{-3X}],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-x+1}, & x\ge 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)={e}^{-3x}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{e}^{-3X}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{e}^{-3x}\cdot {e}^{-x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{e}^{-4x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}[{e}^{-4x+1}]_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(0-{e}^{-3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4{e}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
